paper.title: Learning Terrain-Aware Whole-Body Control for Perceptive Legged Loco-Manipulation

review.question: 2025-07-19 至 2026-07-19 的 loco-manipulation 研究在哪些控制、学习、数据、感知、评测和部署方向取得了可验证进展，其适用边界与未解问题是什么？

relevance.reason: Direct study of perceptive legged loco-manipulation over uneven terrain with simulation and real-robot tests.

sections_read.purpose: Map the terrain-awareness and workspace-coupling problem.
Inspect foot-centric terrain encoding, goal sampling and distillation.

sections_read.locator: IV Experiments > IV-B Simulation Results > IV-B 2 Ablation Study
IV Experiments > IV-C Real-World Deployment > IV-C 2 Long-Horizon Loco-Manipulation
sections_read.purpose: Check the long-horizon cross-terrain demonstration and autonomy boundary.

research_question: Does foot-centric exteroception allow one whole-body controller to preserve reach and stability across uneven terrain?
contributions: Terrain-aware whole-body RL with foot-centric multi-ring elevation encoding and contact-plane-relative end-effector sampling.

method.summary: An asymmetric actor-critic encodes foot-centered terrain samples and tracks goals defined relative to a fitted foot contact plane; policy distillation reduces gradient interference.
assumptions: A reliable elevation map is available from depth and LiDAR.
High-level commands are provided by VR teleoperation.

datasets: Procedurally generated slopes, stairs and discrete obstacles
embodiments: Quadruped manipulator with onboard depth camera and LiDAR
study_context.sample_or_scale: Simulation baseline/ablation tests and a five-run real long-horizon sequence.

evaluation.design: Compares decoupled blind/perceptive locomotion plus IK and ablated whole-body policies on flat and complex terrain, followed by real deployment.

findings.finding: Terrain representation and contact-plane-relative goals jointly expand reach while preserving traversal, but the real task is teleoperated rather than autonomous.
findings.scope: One real robot on a staged stair-and-platform route.
findings.locator: IV Experiments > IV-C Real-World Deployment > IV-C 2 Long-Horizon Loco-Manipulation

author_stated.limitation: A sophisticated high-level policy is still future work for fully autonomous task execution.

reader_inferred.boundary: The five consecutive successes do not establish robustness across outdoor terrain classes or perception failures.
reader_inferred.basis: The real route, objects and sensing stack are fixed and high-level commands come from VR.

transfer_boundary: Supports low-level perceptive whole-body control when terrain elevation is observable; autonomous task reasoning and broader outdoor reliability remain untested.

design_strengths: Includes a continuous real cross-terrain task.
design_risks: Only five consecutive real trials are reported.
The perception stack and route are highly structured.
critical_appraisal.baseline_fairness: Decoupled and blind baselines target the relevant coordination question, although training budgets are not fully normalized in the prose.
critical_appraisal.metric_validity: Stumble, tracking and completion capture control utility; safety claims should not exceed the tested route.
critical_appraisal.reproducibility: Policy inputs and sensing route are described, but the real elevation-mapping details depend on an external framework.
critical_appraisal.external_validity: Limited to terrain that can be represented by the onboard elevation map and a single morphology.

evidence_cards.claim: In a staged real long-horizon task, TA-WBC completed five consecutive bottle-pick, stair-climb, disposal and return runs without falls or stumbles.
evidence_cards.relation: Supports terrain-aware low-level whole-body control for cross-terrain loco-manipulation.
evidence_cards.summary: The real-world section explicitly reports repeated completion of the full multi-stage route.
evidence_cards.source_context: The result shows that the legged manipulator with TA-WBC can successfully finish this long-horizon challenging task 5 times in a row without any falls or stumbles, verifying the robustness of our framework.

quantitative.task_or_sample: bottle pick, five-step stair climb, disposal and return
quantitative.locator: IV Experiments > IV-C Real-World Deployment > IV-C 2 Long-Horizon Loco-Manipulation

verification.rationale: The cited sentence states the exact count, full route and absence of falls or stumbles; the claim does not generalize beyond this staged route.
